claim: The proposed `Reflect → Compound → Scout ⇢ Observe` topology requires a backward FSM transition that does not exist and an Observe ingestion channel that does not exist.

Scout reaches the leading-candidate slot on a trigger — 'unresolved contradiction, or detected shear' — that has no referent in any state record the loop carries, and the charter never requires triggers to be decidable.

None of the eight tournament criteria asks which edge or state variable disappears when the candidate box is deleted, so a candidate already realizable as an existing phase-gated capability can win a phase contest.
Scout's triggers surface in Orient/Reflect but its gate sits after Compound, adding a full cycle of deadtime — and the phase it occupies has no search tools at all.

The charter asserts agent orchestration is an orthogonal topology, then seeds Share — a candidate whose entire content is a change to that topology — so either Share is out of scope by construction or the axiom is false and untested.

The one sentence carrying the review's entire empirical burden names no measured quantity, threshold, cycle count, recorder, or outcome that would favor the no-S null, so the tournament cannot lose and the required confidence figure is unearned.

A 'read-only' pilot is unachievable in this runtime: every candidate turn writes the evidence file that Compound aggregates into the very QualitySignal a pilot would use as its outcome measure — a confounded design.
'Only successful probes may be Compounded' is a selection rule on the wrong variable: it rewards predictions that were never at risk and erases the failed probes that carry the information.

Retirement is specified as a field the artifact carries about itself, with no actor, clock, or sweep that consumes it — and one coarse 'speculative' grade leaves nothing for a sweep to write even if one existed.

Six of eight criteria are phrased as properties of an operation, so no-S scores N/A on most of the matrix; and no output item asks which evidence discriminates between hypotheses, so non-diagnostic evidence will read as support.

Scout, Search, Speculate and Synthesize share one (input, output, consumer) contract and differ only in which facet of the act they name, so the shortlist can rank a single operation three times while calling it a competitive field.

Scout matches this codebase's definition of a capability on every property that distinguishes it from a phase — conditional, unpositioned, artifact-emitting — so the phase claim is carried by the acronym rather than the contract.

The tournament scores candidates against the six phase *names* rather than against the members that already carry their load, so "semantic distinctness" cannot distinguish a new member from a duplicate — and the no-S null is scored as "absence of a phase" instead of "these five members already carry the load".

The `Reflect → Compound → Scout ⇢ Observe` topology draws a tenon into a mortise that does not exist: the phase FSM is a forward-only cursor with no back-edge, and the arrow's target phase (Observe) is the one phase the CLI refuses to start.

The charter's most consequential question — phase vs side-loop vs capability vs artifact type — is posed with no test, though this frame makes the test mechanical: in Skaffen a phase *is* a capability gate, so the discriminator is the gate delta.

Scout is pinned at the wrong end of the beam: placed after the phase that cuts the session's durable artifact, while two of its three stated triggers (unresolved contradiction, detected shear) surface during Orient.

The charter's central safety claim — "scout reports cannot become evidence directly" — is asserted and enforced by nothing, and the runtime it lands in has one ungraded store whose aggregate is read back by Orient, so any candidate that adds a writer without adding a grade field is net-negative against the no-S null.

Scout's "expiration or review condition" specifies demotion as a field on a document — no actor, no act, no store, no trigger — and the runtime makes it unenforceable: the only durable store is append-only and its records have no identifier to re-grade against.

The charter requires forward routing and never requires backward traceability, so the chain terminates at promotion: a compounded lesson keeps no link to probe, report, or source domain, and discrediting a link can never trigger re-grading.

The Falsifiability criterion scores whether a candidate produces probes, not whether a probe's failure is recorded against the source-domain analogy that motivated it, so a source domain's tenth failed borrowing is indistinguishable from its first.

The two fields that make Scout look rigorous — correspondence mapping and where-the-analogy-breaks — carry no validity test: no shared effective cause need be named, and nothing bars transferring from a source claim that is itself ungraded, so the grade attaches to the act of scouting rather than to the strength of the chain behind the claim.

Claim (1) holds as the defect of record and claim (2) is demoted from rival defect to binding runtime constraint: (2) presupposes an outcome measure that (1) correctly observes is never named, so an unspecified pilot has no measure to confound - but (2)'s strongest form is broader than stated, because 'read-only' fails under BOTH its operational and its epistemic readings.

If item 7 is repaired the obvious way and uses the quality signal as its outcome, the two pilot arms are written to different files and never compared: a minimal read-only pilot session is by construction no-write/no-edit/read-heavy, which is exactly inferTaskType's first branch, routing it to docs.jsonl while the no-S null arm routes to feature/bug-fix/refactor.

CONFIRMED, and wider than claimed: the mechanism-to-word substitution is enforced not only by the S-word seeds and the mnemonic criterion but by the box-shaped per-candidate spec, which makes the charter's own mandated control-theory candidate class structurally unenterable, and the substitution cost is never required to be declared.

The runtime's only outcome measure has no dimension in which exploration can pay off within the window Orient reads, so the charter's falsifiable pilot returns a negative verdict on any S candidate regardless of whether it works.

Finding (2) holds and dissolves finding (1): Skaffen's phaseFSM carries no control flow at all — it is an integer index advanced only by a human `/advance` slash command — so a phase reduces to a named capability profile, the gate delta is the discriminator, and Scout's required capability set is a strict subset of Orient's (delta = ∅). The missing backward edge that (1) objects to is a category error, not a defect, because no automatic forward edge exists either.

Pointed symmetrically, the gate-delta discriminator indicts the incumbents: Observe ⊂ Decide ⊂ Orient is a strict 1-2 tool nesting under identical model routing with no enforceable transition, so three of six existing phases fail the 'semantic distinctness' and 'operational crispness' criteria the charter applies to challengers — every ranking against the unexamined no-S baseline is therefore uninterpretable, and the honest recommendation space must include 'merge existing phases'.
